title: FACT CHECK: ICC chamber order on ‘Incident 57’ doesn’t mean Duterte will be released
summary: While the ICC Trial Chamber III did order the removal of ‘Incident 57’ from the list of incidents in the charges against Duterte, this does not mean the entire case itself has been dismissed or that…

blocks.text: Claim: Former president Rodrigo Duterte is set to be released after the International Criminal Court (ICC) dropped one drug-related killing, “Incident 57,” from his crimes against humanity case.

Why we fact-checked this: The Facebook reel bearing the claim has already received 823,000 views, 12,500 reactions, 1,400 shares, and 1,200 comments as of writing. It was posted on November 17 and continues to gain traction up to this date.

The video shows a photo of Vice President Sara Duterte and her father, who is currently detained at the ICC facility in The Hague, Netherlands. The text on the photo reads, “Tuluyan nang ibinasura ng ICC ang Incident 57 drug war charges laban kay PRRD dahil sa sablay ng petsa.”(The ICC has definitively dismissed the ‘Incident 57’ drug war charges against [former president Rodrigo Roa Duterte] due to an error in the date.)
Additional text overlaid on the reel claimed that the ICC junked the case and that the Vice President has urged their supporters to pray for her father’s safety upon his supposed return.

The facts: While the ICC Trial Chamber III’s order to drop “Incident 57” from the list of incidents in the second count of charges against Duterte is genuine, it is not true that he is set to be released following this directive.
Duterte remains detained in ICC custody. There are no credible news reports or official announcements saying that Duterte can now return to the Philippines or that his case has been dismissed.

In an October 9 ruling, the ICC Trial Chamber III ordered prosecutors to remove Incident 57, a single alleged drug-related killing involving a “high-value target,” because it fell outside the confirmed timeframe of the second charge against Duterte.

The prosecution then complied with the order. In a document dated October 20, the prosecution said that all references to Incident 57 are now removed from the trial brief and replaced with redacted information.

Duterte is currently facing three counts of crimes against humanity, including murders in and around Davao City allegedly committed by the “Davao Death Squad” while he served as mayor between 2013 and 2016, targeted killings of alleged high-value targets during his presidency between 2016 and 2017, and murders and attempted murders during barangay-level anti-drug operations between 2016 and 2018.

List of incidents: Aside from Incident 57, which the ICC chamber ordered removed, there are many other active incidents included in the charges against Duterte. In October, the ICC trial chamber approved the addition of seven new incidents to the charges, raising the total number from 49 to 56.
Duterte was arrested in March 2025 for crimes against humanity. He is set to face trial on November 30.Previous fact checks: Rappler has fact-checked similar false claims about Duterte’s detention:
